---
title: Administration and operator service
description: Bind scoped HostFn deployment operations to a host-owned control plane.
---

The HostFn CLI deploys an application from a developer or CI machine. The separate `hostfn/operator` entry point and `@hostfn/admin` package let a host application expose deployment administration through Super Console. The capability is a contract; it does not provision a control plane by itself.

## What the host supplies

`HostFnOperatorService` takes a `HostFnOperatorStore` and a `HostFnDeploymentExecutor`. The store owns targets, deployments, domains, and variable metadata. `putVariable(variable, secretValue)` also receives the plaintext secret before the executor runs, and the memory store may retain it. Production stores must protect retained values at rest, restrict access, and avoid logging them—or deliberately avoid persisting the value while preserving the metadata required by the store contract. The executor performs external deploy, cancel, rollback, restart, domain, and variable effects. `MemoryHostFnOperatorStore` is a reference store for development and single-process installations; use a durable implementation for a production control plane.

Every operator record carries an `installationId`, `workspaceId`, `projectId`, and `environmentId` scope. The host must derive the active scope from the authenticated admin context and enforce authorization before invoking the adapter. Domain attachment uses an immutable identity and a reclaimable work lease so retries do not attach the same hostname to a different target. The external executor must be idempotent for retries with the same domain ID.

## Capability resources and actions

| Resource | Reads | Actions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Targets | List and get | Restart |
| Deployments | List and get | Deploy, cancel, rollback |
| Domains | List | Attach, detach |
| Variables | List keys | Set, delete |

Variable values are never returned by the list operation. Target server addresses are marked sensitive in the capability. Read and write operations have separate permissions. Destructive actions, including variable deletion, require MFA confirmation; variable setting requires recent authentication; deploy and domain attach require explicit confirmation for their external effects. These are declared confirmation requirements: the host must supply a confirmation service whose verifier validates the requested method and `maxAgeSeconds` freshness. The dispatcher only checks the verifier’s boolean decision; a permissive verifier does not enforce MFA or recent authentication. All writes require audit evidence through the shared admin dispatcher.

## Binding the adapter

Create an operator service with your store and executor, then pass it to `createHostFnOperatorAdminService` and `createHostFnAdminAdapter` from `@hostfn/admin`. The host must connect the adapter to its authenticated Super Console dispatcher and supply the active environment scope. The [operator source](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/hostfn/cli/src/operator.ts) and [admin capability](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/hostfn/admin/src/index.ts) define the exact interfaces and operation IDs.

Use the complete [SuperConsoleOptions and service interfaces](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/superconsole/src/lib/server/types.ts) for the binding: register the adapter in `adapters`, include `hostfn` in `enabledModules`, and implement the operator-auth provider's `authenticate` and `authorizeScope` methods as well as the mutation hook below. Keep the bundled console's default `/api/admin/v1` base path. Supply `openApiSecuritySchemes` with both `operatorSession` and `operatorApiKey` describing your authentication provider.

Every HostFn write is declared idempotent. Supply a durable store implementing the complete [AdminIdempotencyStore interface](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/packages/admin/src/idempotency.ts): `begin`, `complete`, `release`, `finalizeAudit`, `prepareCompensation`, `claimCompensation`, and `releaseCompensation`. The initial Super Console presence check inspects only the first three methods; the dispatcher constructor also requires the terminal-audit reconciliation and compensation hooks, even before an operation uses them. Implement their atomic, claim-fenced transitions and retry semantics as specified in the interface; no-op hooks do not satisfy the production contract.

Pass an idempotency key with each write request. A standalone dispatcher returns `dependency_unavailable` without a store and `precondition_failed` without a key; `createSuperConsole` rejects a missing store at startup. The operator store's domain lease protects one domain workflow but does not replace dispatcher idempotency across all mutations.

Supply a durable [AdminAuditSink](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/packages/admin/src/audit.ts) with `write` and `idempotentById: true`. The dispatcher rejects a sink without this capability marker at construction. Writes must be durable and first-write-wins by event ID, including retries after a lost acknowledgement; setting the marker alone does not provide those guarantees. Configure this sink alongside the confirmation service and authorization policies before exposing operations.

When binding through `createSuperConsole`, the operator-auth provider must implement `auth.authorizeMutation({ principal, request })`. Startup rejects the configuration without this hook because HostFn exposes mutations. The hook must reject unauthorized mutation requests; an `AdminPolicyEvaluator` does not replace this operator-auth check. Supply `shellPolicy.authorize` for console-surface access as well as the dispatcher's operation policy for scope and permission checks. These are separate authorization boundaries, not interchangeable services.

Also provide a `SuperConsoleConfirmationService`, not only a verifier. It must implement `issue`, `prepareActivation`, `cancelActivation`, `activate`, `revoke`, and `verify`; Super Console checks these methods at startup because HostFn mutations require confirmation. A token remains unusable while staged, and activation follows durable audit preparation. The service must keep cancellation and revocation effective so a denied or abandoned token cannot later authorize a write.

This integration is distinct from the CLI deployment flow. Review [deployment locks](/docs/documentation/advanced/deployment-locks), [rollbacks](/docs/documentation/advanced/rollback), and [environment variables](/docs/documentation/environment/overview) as background on the CLI implementation. The operator service delegates these effects to `HostFnDeploymentExecutor`; it does not inherit the CLI’s remote lock files, backup-based rollback, or `.env` layout. The host must implement any corresponding concurrency, recovery, and secret-handling guarantees in its executor and control plane.

The store owns targets, deployments, domains, and variable metadata. `putVariable(variable, secretValue)` also receives the plaintext secret before the executor runs, and the memory store may retain it. Production stores must protect retained values at rest, restrict access, and avoid logging them—or deliberately avoid persisting the value while preserving the metadata required by the store contract. The executor performs external deploy, cancel, rollback, restart, domain, and variable effects. `MemoryHostFnOperatorStore` is a reference store for development and single-process installations; use a durable implementation for a production control plane.

Every operator record carries an `installationId`, `workspaceId`, `projectId`, and `environmentId` scope. The host must derive the active scope from the authenticated admin context and enforce authorization before invoking the adapter. Domain attachment uses an immutable identity and a reclaimable work lease so retries do not attach the same hostname to a different target. The external executor must be idempotent for retries with the same domain ID.

## Capability resources and actions

| Resource | Reads | Actions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Targets | List and get | Restart |
| Deployments | List and get | Deploy, cancel, rollback |
| Domains | List | Attach, detach |
| Variables | List keys | Set, delete |

Variable values are never returned by the list operation. Target server addresses are marked sensitive in the capability. Read and write operations have separate permissions. Destructive actions, including variable deletion, require MFA confirmation; variable setting requires recent authentication; deploy and domain attach require explicit confirmation for their external effects. These are declared confirmation requirements: the host must supply a confirmation service whose verifier validates the requested method and `maxAgeSeconds` freshness. The dispatcher only checks the verifier’s boolean decision; a permissive verifier does not enforce MFA or recent authentication. All writes require audit evidence through the shared admin dispatcher.

## Binding the adapter

Create an operator service with your store and executor, then pass it to `createHostFnOperatorAdminService` and `createHostFnAdminAdapter` from `@hostfn/admin`. The host must connect the adapter to its authenticated Super Console dispatcher and supply the active environment scope. The [operator source](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/hostfn/cli/src/operator.ts) and [admin capability](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/hostfn/admin/src/index.ts) define the exact interfaces and operation IDs.

Use the complete [SuperConsoleOptions and service interfaces](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/superconsole/src/lib/server/types.ts) for the binding: register the adapter in `adapters`, include `hostfn` in `enabledModules`, and implement the operator-auth provider's `authenticate` and `authorizeScope` methods as well as the mutation hook below. Keep the bundled console's default `/api/admin/v1` base path. Supply `openApiSecuritySchemes` with both `operatorSession` and `operatorApiKey` describing your authentication provider.

Every HostFn write is declared idempotent. Supply a durable store implementing the complete [AdminIdempotencyStore interface](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/packages/admin/src/idempotency.ts): `begin`, `complete`, `release`, `finalizeAudit`, `prepareCompensation`, `claimCompensation`, and `releaseCompensation`. The initial Super Console presence check inspects only the first three methods; the dispatcher constructor also requires the terminal-audit reconciliation and compensation hooks, even before an operation uses them. Implement their atomic, claim-fenced transitions and retry semantics as specified in the interface; no-op hooks do not satisfy the production contract.

Pass an idempotency key with each write request. A standalone dispatcher returns `dependency_unavailable` without a store and `precondition_failed` without a key; `createSuperConsole` rejects a missing store at startup. The operator store's domain lease protects one domain workflow but does not replace dispatcher idempotency across all mutations.

Supply a durable [AdminAuditSink](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/packages/admin/src/audit.ts) with `write` and `idempotentById: true`. The dispatcher rejects a sink without this capability marker at construction. Writes must be durable and first-write-wins by event ID, including retries after a lost acknowledgement; setting the marker alone does not provide those guarantees. Configure this sink alongside the confirmation service and authorization policies before exposing operations.

When binding through `createSuperConsole`, the operator-auth provider must implement `auth.authorizeMutation({ principal, request })`. Startup rejects the configuration without this hook because HostFn exposes mutations. The hook must reject unauthorized mutation requests; an `AdminPolicyEvaluator` does not replace this operator-auth check. Supply `shellPolicy.authorize` for console-surface access as well as the dispatcher's operation policy for scope and permission checks. These are separate authorization boundaries, not interchangeable services.

Also provide a `SuperConsoleConfirmationService`, not only a verifier. It must implement `issue`, `prepareActivation`, `cancelActivation`, `activate`, `revoke`, and `verify`; Super Console checks these methods at startup because HostFn mutations require confirmation. A token remains unusable while staged, and activation follows durable audit preparation. The service must keep cancellation and revocation effective so a denied or abandoned token cannot later authorize a write.

This integration is distinct from the CLI deployment flow. Review [deployment locks](/docs/documentation/advanced/deployment-locks), [rollbacks](/docs/documentation/advanced/rollback), and [environment variables](/docs/documentation/environment/overview) as background on the CLI implementation. The operator service delegates these effects to `HostFnDeploymentExecutor`; it does not inherit the CLI’s remote lock files, backup-based rollback, or `.env` layout. The host must implement any corresponding concurrency, recovery, and secret-handling guarantees in its executor and control plane.

=== DEV README
# botfn monorepo

[![Tests](https://github.com/21nOrg/botfn/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/21nOrg/botfn/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/21nOrg/botfn/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/21nOrg/botfn)

Turborepo-based monorepo for bot implementations with platform-agnostic architecture.

## structure

```
.
├── bots/
│   └── discord-bot/          # Discord bot with GitHub and Linear integration
│   └── [more bots...]        # Additional bot implementations
├── packages/
│   ├── discord-core/         # Discord-specific utilities and verification
│   ├── github-integration/   # GitHub API helpers
│   ├── linear-integration/   # Linear API helpers
│   └── shared-types/         # Shared TypeScript types and Zod schemas
├── AGENTS.md                 # Architecture documentation
├── package.json              # Root workspace config
└── turbo.json                # Turborepo pipeline config
```

## getting started

### install dependencies

```bash
npm install
```

### develop a bot

```bash
cd bots/discord-bot
npm run dev
```

### build all packages

```bash
npm run build
```

## npm package boundaries

The shared-types, discord-core, github-integration and linear-integration
packages ship compiled ESM with TypeScript declarations. Their builds and tests
use package-local compiler settings and declared test dependencies; they do not
resolve sibling workspace source.

The Discord bot's minimum npm prerequisite set is:

- `@superfunctions/botfn-shared-types`
- `@superfunctions/botfn-discord-core`
- `@superfunctions/botfn-github-integration`
- `@superfunctions/botfn-linear-integration`
- `@superfunctions/botfn-persistence-service`

These five foundations have no dependencies on each other and may be released in
any order before installing or releasing `@superfunctions/botfn-discord-bot`. Slack core is
independent of the Discord closure and exports both ESM and CommonJS.

Slack request verification accepts canonical decimal Unix-second timestamps only,
checks that the value is a safe integer, and rejects requests more than 300 seconds
from the current time in either direction. It verifies the HMAC against the original
request body without consuming it; the private Slack app can then dispatch signed events.

Run `npm install --workspaces=false`, `npm run build`, `npm test` and
`npm pack --dry-run` from an isolated copy of each package to check its release
boundary. Build before packing: npm exports point at `dist`, not TypeScript source.
Use `@superfunctions/botfn-persistence-service/client` for the public persistence client;
deep imports into the package's source tree are not supported.

BotFn's npm libraries live in the controlled `@superfunctions` organization.
The npm user scope `@botfn` belongs to an unrelated account; old namespace
references and release slugs are removed, not retained as aliases.


## testing

This repository has comprehensive test coverage using Vitest:

- **119 tests** across 4 packages
- **Unit tests** for core functionality
- **Integration tests** with MSW for API mocking  
- **CI/CD** integration with GitHub Actions

Run tests:
```bash
npm test                 # Run all tests
npm run test:coverage    # With coverage report
```

See [TESTING.md](./TESTING.md) for detailed testing guidelines.

## architecture

See [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) for detailed architecture documentation.

### key principles

- **Platform-agnostic core logic**: Business logic in `core.ts` is reusable across platforms
- **Multi-platform deployment**: Deploy to Cloudflare Workers, Digital Ocean, Vercel, etc.
- **Shared packages**: Common utilities and types in workspace packages
- **Type-safe validation**: Zod schemas for runtime validation
- **Monorepo tooling**: Turborepo for efficient builds and caching

## technology stack

- **Framework**: [Hono](https://hono.dev/)
- **Validation**: [Zod](https://zod.dev/)
- **Monorepo**: [Turborepo](https://turbo.build/)
- **Runtime**: Cloudflare Workers, Node.js (adaptable)

## adding a new bot

1. Create bot directory: `mkdir -p bots/my-bot/src`
2. Follow the structure in [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md)
3. Create `core.ts` with business logic
4. Create platform-specific entry points (e.g., `index.cloudflare.ts`)
5. Add workspace dependencies to `package.json`

## deployment

Each bot can be deployed independently:

### Cloudflare Workers

```bash
cd bots/discord-bot
npm run deploy
```

### other platforms

See [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) for Digital Ocean and Vercel deployment guides.
=== PR README
# BotFn

BotFn is the Superfunctions workspace for Discord and Slack bots. Packages live at `botfn/<pkg>` in this repository — not a standalone Turborepo, and not a `bots/` + `packages/` tree.

Bots deploy to **Cloudflare Workers** only.

## Packages

| Path | Package | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |

## structure

```
.
├── bots/
│   └── discord-bot/          # Discord bot with GitHub and Linear integration
│   └── [more bots...]        # Additional bot implementations
├── packages/
│   ├── discord-core/         # Discord-specific utilities and verification
│   ├── github-integration/   # GitHub API helpers
│   ├── linear-integration/   # Linear API helpers
│   └── shared-types/         # Shared TypeScript types and Zod schemas
├── AGENTS.md                 # Architecture documentation
├── package.json              # Root workspace config
└── turbo.json                # Turborepo pipeline config
```

## getting started

### install dependencies

```bash
npm install
```

### develop a bot

```bash
cd bots/discord-bot
npm run dev
```

### build all packages

```bash
npm run build
```

## npm package boundaries

The shared-types, discord-core, github-integration and linear-integration
packages ship compiled ESM with TypeScript declarations. Their builds and tests
use package-local compiler settings and declared test dependencies; they do not
resolve sibling workspace source.

The Discord bot's minimum npm prerequisite set is:

- `@superfunctions/botfn-shared-types`
- `@superfunctions/botfn-discord-core`
- `@superfunctions/botfn-github-integration`
- `@superfunctions/botfn-linear-integration`
- `@superfunctions/botfn-persistence-service`

These five foundations have no dependencies on each other and may be released in
any order before installing or releasing `@superfunctions/botfn-discord-bot`. Slack core is
independent of the Discord closure and exports both ESM and CommonJS.

Slack request verification accepts canonical decimal Unix-second timestamps only,
checks that the value is a safe integer, and rejects requests more than 300 seconds
from the current time in either direction. It verifies the HMAC against the original
request body without consuming it; the private Slack app can then dispatch signed events.

Run `npm install --workspaces=false`, `npm run build`, `npm test` and
`npm pack --dry-run` from an isolated copy of each package to check its release
boundary. Build before packing: npm exports point at `dist`, not TypeScript source.
Use `@superfunctions/botfn-persistence-service/client` for the public persistence client;
deep imports into the package's source tree are not supported.

BotFn's npm libraries live in the controlled `@superfunctions` organization.
The npm user scope `@botfn` belongs to an unrelated account; old namespace
references and release slugs are removed, not retained as aliases.


## testing

This repository has comprehensive test coverage using Vitest:

- **119 tests** across 4 packages
- **Unit tests** for core functionality
- **Integration tests** with MSW for API mocking  
- **CI/CD** integration with GitHub Actions

Run tests:
```bash
npm test                 # Run all tests
npm run test:coverage    # With coverage report
```

See [TESTING.md](./TESTING.md) for detailed testing guidelines.

## architecture

See [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) for detailed architecture documentation.

### key principles

- **Platform-agnostic core logic**: Business logic in `core.ts` is reusable across platforms
- **Multi-platform deployment**: Deploy to Cloudflare Workers, Digital Ocean, Vercel, etc.
- **Shared packages**: Common utilities and types in workspace packages
- **Type-safe validation**: Zod schemas for runtime validation
- **Monorepo tooling**: Turborepo for efficient builds and caching

## technology stack

- **Framework**: [Hono](https://hono.dev/)
- **Validation**: [Zod](https://zod.dev/)
- **Monorepo**: [Turborepo](https://turbo.build/)
- **Runtime**: Cloudflare Workers, Node.js (adaptable)

## adding a new bot

1. Create bot directory: `mkdir -p bots/my-bot/src`
2. Follow the structure in [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md)
3. Create `core.ts` with business logic
4. Create platform-specific entry points (e.g., `index.cloudflare.ts`)
5. Add workspace dependencies to `package.json`

## deployment

Each bot can be deployed independently:

### Cloudflare Workers

```bash
cd bots/discord-bot
npm run deploy
```

### other platforms

See [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) for Digital Ocean and Vercel deployment guides.

Plugins implement named callbacks on `DatafnPlugin`; there is no event subscription array. `runsOn` selects the client, server, or both. Register the object with `plugins: [plugin]` when creating the client or server.

## Hook context and arguments

```typescript
import type { DatafnHookContext, DatafnPlugin } from "@datafn/core";

export const auditPlugin: DatafnPlugin = {
  name: "audit-mutations",
  runsOn: ["server"],
  beforeMutation(ctx, mutation) {
    console.log("before mutation", ctx.env, mutation);
    return mutation;
  },
  afterMutation(ctx, mutation, result) {
    console.log("after mutation", ctx.env, mutation, result);
    // This callback observes the result; its return value is ignored by the caller.
  },
};
```

`DatafnHookContext` contains `env: "client" | "server"`, `schema: DatafnSchema`, and optional host `context`. It does not contain an event name, resource filter, or payload. The operation payload is a separate argument. Treat `context` and payloads as unknown until narrowed by application code.

#!/bin/bash

done

for PR in "$@"; do $S/status.sh $PR; done
EOF

Use `runtime.browser.call(...)` for Promise-first calls, `runtime.browser.namespace(...)` for a specific API namespace, and `runtime.browser.raw` only when raw behavior is needed. Branch on `runtime.capabilities` for side panel, offscreen, and scripting support. The runtime does not grant browser permissions; declare and justify them in extension config and generated manifests.

Use `runtime.rpc`, `runtime.events`, and `runtime.ports` to communicate across extension contexts. Define background handlers in the service worker and avoid putting domain authority in a content script. # MCP server

The authfn **MCP server** is a small Node process that wraps the docs as a set of tools. MCP-aware assistants (Claude Desktop, Cursor, custom hosts) connect to it once, then have on-demand access to:

- All doc pages, by slug or full-text search.
- The OpenAPI spec — operation lookup by id, route, or tag.
- Example apps — file listings, content reads.
- Skill packs — see [Skills](./skills).

# Brief: bring one DocsFn site PR onto the shared docs-site runtime in dev

You own exactly one PR in `21nCo/superfunctions` (GitHub; use `GH_CONFIG_DIR=~/.config/gh-other` for every `gh` call). The PR adds a DocsFn/SvelteKit docs site under `<pkg>/docs`. Your job is to make it merge-ready against current `dev` and drive automated PR review to zero valid findings. **Do not merge the PR.** Report back when done.

## Context
- PR #213 (ExtFn) landed the canonical shared runtime on `dev`: `scripts/docs-site/**`, the AuthFn/FileFn sites migrated onto it, `scripts/cloudflare-docs/**` product registry, the docs deploy/routes workflows, `turbo.json` (`globalDependencies` includes `scripts/docs-site/**`).
- Every other docs PR (yours included) carries its own older, diverged copy of those shared files. They must now take **dev's** version and drop their own.
- Dev docs hosting convention (from dev's `scripts/cloudflare-docs/config.mjs`): dev host `<pkg>.21n.site` on the shared `21n.site` zone in the 21n-dev account; live host/zone is the product's own domain (keep whatever live host the PR already used, e.g. `<pkg>.com`).
- Use ExtFn (`extfn/docs`) on dev as the reference consumer: `src/lib/server/docs-site-source.ts`, `vite.config.ts` (uses `docsSiteCorePlugin`), `svelte.config.js` (`@site/docs-search` alias), `tsconfig.json` (`@site/docs-search` path), `package.json` scripts (`test`, `check:llms`, `generate:llms`), `scripts/generate-llms.mjs`, prerendered `/docs/llms.txt` + `/docs/llms-full.txt` routes.

## Steps
1. Worktree: `git -C /Volumes/Dev/n/superfunctions fetch origin dev <branch>` then `git -C /Volumes/Dev/n/superfunctions worktree add --detach /Volumes/Dev/n/sfn-wt/<pkg> origin/<branch>`. Path normalization error in `scripts/docs-site/runtime.ts`: the root cleanup regex strips the leading dot from `.content`, so with `content.root: ".content"`, `collectionDirectory` searches for `content/...` while bundled module keys retain `.content/...`, causing `collectEntriesForCollection` to silently exclude the collection. Remove only an exact `.` segment or a `./` prefix.
```typescript
const normalizedRoot = normalizeProviderPath(config.content.root ?? ".");
const root = (normalizedRoot === "." ? "" : normalizedRoot.replace(/^\.\//, "")).replace(/\/+$/, "");
```

 +[`llms.txt`](https://llmstxt.org/) is a community convention for static, LLM-friendly summaries of a project. authfn serves **two** files under `/docs`:
 +
 +- `https://authfn.com/docs/llms.txt` — short index. Lists every doc page with a one-line description and a link.
 +- `https://authfn.com/docs/llms-full.txt` — full text. Concatenated markdown of every doc page plus the OpenAPI spec.
++=======
+ [`llms.txt`](https://llmstxt.org/) is a convention for LLM-friendly project context. This docs site serves two generated files under its existing `/docs` mount:
  
- Use whichever fits your assistant's context budget.
+ - `https://authfn.com/docs/llms.txt` — short page index.
+ - `https://authfn.com/docs/llms-full.txt` — full documentation context, including the configured API material.
++>>>>>>> origin/dev
  
- ## How they're generated
+ These are the configured publication URLs; a local build does not prove live hosting or credentials.
  
- Both files are emitted by docsfn at build time:
+ ## Generation
  
+ The normal repository build prepares AuthFn's physical dependencies before regenerating OpenAPI and LLM content:
+ 
++<<<<<<< HEAD
 +```bash
 +npm run generate:llms --workspace=@authfn/docs
++=======
+ ```sh
+ npm exec -- turbo run build --filter=@authfn/docs
++>>>>>>> origin/dev
  ```
  
- The pipeline:
+ After those prerequisites are built, run from `authfn/docs`:
+ 
+ ```sh
+ npm run generate:openapi
+ npm run generate:llms
+ npm run check:llms
+ ```
  
- 1. Walks every page in `content/docs/**`.
- 2. For each page, extracts the H1 + frontmatter description for `llms.txt`.
- 3. For each page, includes the full markdown body for `llms-full.txt`.
- 4. Appends the OpenAPI spec from `content/api/authfn.json` (operations + schemas).
- 5. Writes both files into `static/` so they ship with the deployed site.
+ `generate:llms` loads `docsfn.config.ts` through the consumer's published DocsFn package and filesystem provider, builds the manifest, and writes `static/llms.txt` and `static/llms-full.txt`. Native prerendered routes publish those files at `/docs/llms.txt` and `/docs/llms-full.txt`; the app-root static copies are not the advertised docs-owner URLs. `check:llms` compares generated content without writing it.
  
  ## Use it

---
title: AI Resources
description: First-class integrations for LLM-based coding assistants — llms.txt, an MCP server, and per-tool skill packs.
---

# AI Resources

authfn ships with **first-class AI assistant support** so the LLM in your editor can answer questions, generate idiomatic code, and apply correct patterns.

These integrations are powered by [docsfn](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/tree/dev/docsfn) — the same engine that builds this documentation site — so every doc page is automatically available to your assistant.

## What's available

| Resource | Use it when… |
| --- | --- |
| [llms.txt](./llms-txt) | You want a single-file context dump for Cursor / Claude / Codex / GPTs / etc. |
| [MCP server](./mcp) | You're using an MCP-aware assistant (Claude Desktop, Cursor with MCP, custom hosts) and want live retrieval. |
| [Skills](./skills) | You want to teach an assistant a specific authfn pattern (sign-in flow, social OAuth, multi-region, …). |
| [Cursor](./cursor) | You're on Cursor and want one-click setup. |
| [Claude](./claude) | You're on Claude Desktop / Claude Code and want one-click setup. |
| [Codex / Droid](./codex) | You're on Factory Codex / Droid (or any AGENTS.md-aware tool). |

## How they fit together

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Docs["Docs source\n(content/docs/**)"]
    OpenAPI["OpenAPI spec\n(content/api/authfn.json)"]
    Examples["Example apps\n(authfn/examples)"]

    Docs --> LlmsTxt["llms.txt + llms-full.txt"]
    OpenAPI --> LlmsTxt
    Examples --> LlmsTxt

    Docs --> MCP["MCP server"]
    OpenAPI --> MCP
    Examples --> MCP

    Docs --> Skills["Skill packs"]

    LlmsTxt --> Editor["Editor / Assistant"]
    MCP --> Editor
    Skills --> Editor
```

The same content powers all three surfaces; each is the right shape for a different consumer.

## Quick start

The fastest way to get going is to point your assistant at the canonical URL:

```
https://authfn.com/docs/llms-full.txt
```

Most assistants will accept that as a context source. If your tool is MCP-aware, see [MCP](./mcp) for a richer experience that surfaces type definitions, route metadata, and example apps on demand.
---
title: Skills
description: Packaged authfn patterns your assistant can apply on request — sign-in flows, OAuth, multi-region, and more.
---

# Skills

A **skill** is a small, self-contained context pack: prompt, sample code, and links to the relevant doc pages. Your assistant can call `authfn.skills.invoke` with a skill name and the user's request; the response is a focused playbook, not a full RAG dump.

Skills are how you prevent your assistant from synthesizing an outdated or wrong-shaped solution.

## Bundled skills

| Skill | When the assistant should pick it |
| --- | --- |
| `add-password-auth` | "Add email/password sign-in to my app." |
| `add-otp-sign-in` | "Add magic-link or OTP sign-in." |
| `add-social-oauth` | "Let users sign in with Google / Apple / GitHub." |
| `add-2fa` | "Enable two-factor auth." |
| `add-api-keys` | "Issue API keys for our CLI." |
| `add-multi-region` | "Set up authfn in EU + US." |
| `add-native-handoff` | "Hand off web sign-in to my iOS app." |
| `migrate-from-better-auth` | "Move from Better Auth." |
| `migrate-from-clerk` | "Move from Clerk." |
| `migrate-from-authjs` | "Move from Auth.js / NextAuth." |

## Anatomy of a skill

```jsonc
{
  "id": "add-2fa",
  "title": "Add 2FA to an existing authfn app",
  "applicability": ["authfn", "two-factor"],
  "context": [
    "docs/plugins/two-factor.md",
    "docs/recipes/adding-2fa.md"
  ],
  "playbook": [
    "1. Install: `npm install authfn @authfn/two-factor @authfn/client`",
    "2. Add `authFnTwoFactorPlugin()` to `authfn({ plugins: authFnPlugins(...) })`.",
    "3. Generate schema: `npx @superfunctions/cli generate-schema --config ./superfunctions.config.mjs --adapter drizzle --dialect postgres --output ./db/generated --force`.",
    "4. Pass `encryptionKeyResolver` under `createServer({ pluginRuntime: { twoFactor } })`.",
    "5. UI: enroll → confirm → challenge. See recipes/adding-2fa.md."
  ]
}
```

When invoked, the assistant gets:

- The full text of every `context` page.
- The structured `playbook`.
- The user's question.

…and is told to produce code that follows the playbook precisely.

  "id": "my-skill",
  "title": "My custom skill",

# Skills

A **skill** is a small, self-contained context pack: prompt, sample code, and links to the relevant doc pages. Your assistant can call `authfn.skills.invoke` with a skill name and the user's request; the response is a focused playbook, not a full RAG dump.

Skills are how you prevent your assistant from synthesizing an outdated or wrong-shaped solution.

## Bundled skills

| Skill | When the assistant should pick it |
| --- | --- |
| `add-password-auth` | "Add email/password sign-in to my app." |
| `add-otp-sign-in` | "Add magic-link or OTP sign-in." |
| `add-social-oauth` | "Let users sign in with Google / Apple / GitHub." |
| `add-2fa` | "Enable two-factor auth." |
| `add-api-keys` | "Issue API keys for our CLI." |
| `add-multi-region` | "Set up authfn in EU + US." |
| `add-native-handoff` | "Hand off web sign-in to my iOS app." |
| `migrate-from-better-auth` | "Move from Better Auth." |
| `migrate-from-clerk` | "Move from Clerk." |
| `migrate-from-authjs` | "Move from Auth.js / NextAuth." |

## Anatomy of a skill

```jsonc
{
  "id": "add-2fa",
  "title": "Add 2FA to an existing authfn app",
  "applicability": ["authfn", "two-factor"],
  "context": [
    "docs/plugins/two-factor.md",
    "docs/recipes/adding-2fa.md"
  ],
  "playbook": [
    "1. Install: `npm install authfn @authfn/two-factor @authfn/client`",
    "2. Add `authFnTwoFactorPlugin()` to `authfn({ plugins: authFnPlugins(...) })`.",
    "3. Generate schema: `npx @superfunctions/cli generate-schema --config ./superfunctions.config.mjs --adapter drizzle --dialect postgres --output ./db/generated --force`.",
    "4. Pass `encryptionKeyResolver` under `createServer({ pluginRuntime: { twoFactor } })`.",
    "5. UI: enroll → confirm → challenge. See recipes/adding-2fa.md."
  ]
}
```

When invoked, the assistant gets:

- The full text of every `context` page.
- The structured `playbook`.
- The user's question.

…and is told to produce code that follows the playbook precisely.

# Claude

## Claude Desktop

Add this to `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` (macOS) or `%AppData%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` (Windows):

```jsonc
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "authfn": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@authfn/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Restart Claude Desktop. Type `/` and you'll see the authfn tools.

Claude will pick up the MCP server automatically and answer questions about authfn with up-to-date docs and OpenAPI awareness.

## Claude Code

Claude Code reads MCP from a project-local file. From your project root:

```jsonc
// .claude/mcp.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "authfn": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@authfn/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

## Adding context

If you want Claude to *always* know what stack you're on, add a project-level CLAUDE.md:

```markdown
# Project

This is a SvelteKit app using:
- `authfn` for the auth kernel (mounted at /auth)
- `@authfn/password` and `@authfn/email-otp` for sign-in methods
- @authfn/client + @authfn/svelte for the browser
- Postgres + Drizzle for the database

When you need to know how something in @authfn/* works, use the `authfn.*` MCP tools.
For migration questions, invoke the appropriate `authfn.skills.*` skill.
```

## llms.txt fallback

For one-off conversations, paste this into a Claude prompt:

```text
Reference docs: https://authfn.com/docs/llms-full.txt

Now help me…
```

Claude will fetch and use the file as context.

## Related

- [MCP](./mcp)
- [Skills](./skills)

# Codex / Droid (and any AGENTS.md-aware tool)

The [AGENTS.md](https://agents.md) convention is supported by Factory's Codex and Droid CLIs as well as several other agentic tools. Drop an `AGENTS.md` at the root of your repo with a section dedicated to authfn.

## Repo-root AGENTS.md

```markdown
# Project Agents

## authfn

When working with `@authfn/*`:

- Mount path is `/auth`.
- Plugins enabled: password, email-otp, social-oauth (Google), 2FA, api-keys.
- Database is Postgres via Drizzle.
- The schema is generated by `npx @superfunctions/cli generate-schema --config ./superfunctions.config.mjs --adapter drizzle --dialect postgres --output ./apps/api/src/db/generated --force` and lives in `apps/api/src/db/generated/authfn-schema.ts`.

Authoritative docs: https://authfn.com/docs
For a full-text RAG file: https://authfn.com/docs/llms-full.txt

If you have access to MCP tools (`authfn.docs.search`, `authfn.openapi.operation`, `authfn.skills.invoke`), prefer those.
```

## Factory Droid MCP setup

## llms.txt fallback

If you'd rather not run an MCP server, point Cursor at the static file:

```text
---
description: authfn
---

When working with @authfn/*, fetch context from https://authfn.com/docs/llms-full.txt as needed.
```

## Project-specific tweaks

Inside `.cursor/rules/authfn.mdc`, add anything specific to your stack:

```markdown
This project uses `authfn` with the `@authfn/password` and `@authfn/email-otp` plugins.
The kernel is mounted in `apps/api/src/auth.ts`.
The client lives in `packages/sdk/src/auth.ts`.

When generating sign-in / sign-up code, use the `client.*` helpers from `packages/sdk/src/auth.ts`.
```

## Tips

- Keep rules short. Longer = more cost per turn.
- Mention your **mount path** explicitly. authfn doesn't care if it's `/auth` or `/api/auth`, but the assistant might guess wrong.
- Mention which plugins are enabled. The assistant won't suggest `signInWithPassword` if it knows you only have OTP.

## Related

- [MCP](./mcp)
- [llms.txt](./llms-txt)

content.content:
---
title: Administration
description: Bind FileFn's scoped Super Console capability to an authorized principal.
---

# Administration

`@filefn/admin` exposes a Super Console capability over FileFn's public domain services. A host application supplies a configured `FileFn` facade and maps each authorized admin actor and scope to a FileFn `principalId` and optional `tenantId`.

```ts
import { createFileFnAdminAdapter, createFileFnDomainAdminService } from "@filefn/admin";

const service = createFileFnDomainAdminService({
  fileFn,
  context: (adminContext) => resolveAuthorizedFileFnContext(adminContext),
});
const adapter = createFileFnAdminAdapter(service);
```

`resolveAuthorizedFileFnContext` is host code. It must derive a principal from the authenticated scope; the domain service rejects a missing `principalId`. Mount the adapter through the shared admin dispatcher with its permission, confirmation, and audit policies. The capability requires at least project scope.

## Resources and actions

The capability covers files, versions, upload sessions, grants, share links, policies, and processing artifacts. Child resources such as versions, grants, shares, and artifacts are listed under an authorized file. Operations include authorized downloads, file deletion, upload creation/completion/abort, grant and share creation/revocation, and artifact processing.

File deletion requires MFA confirmation and removes the file's versions, artifacts, grants, and shares. Other writes carry their own risk and confirmation metadata; the host must enforce the capability's declared policy and write audit records. Upload tokens, storage keys, share tokens, provider URLs and headers, and policy storage paths are sensitive and must not leak through list responses.

For an admin download, standard FileFn download services normally produce a signed URL or application proxy descriptor. It rejects provider request headers instead of exposing them to a browser. Review [downloads](/docs/features/downloads), [grants](/docs/features/grants), and [share links](/docs/features/share-links) for the underlying FileFn access rules.

The [capability source](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/filefn/admin/src/index.ts) defines operation IDs and schemas. The [domain service](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/filefn/admin/src/domain-service.ts) shows how the public FileFn facade enforces ownership and creates safe responses.

The admin service itself only rejects descriptors with non-empty provider headers; it does not validate a URL’s origin or signature. Hosts using custom storage/download services must ensure that every returned header-free URL is safe for the intended client and authorization scope.
__tests__
domain-service.ts
index.ts

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Register a SvelteKit DocsFn site in the Cloudflare docs deploy config, mirroring extfn.

usage: register-site.py <repo> <pkg> <live-domain>
"""
import re
import sys

repo, pkg, live = sys.argv[1:4]
upper = re.sub(r"[^A-Z0-9]+", "_", live.upper())


def edit(rel, fn):
    path = f"{repo}/{rel}"
    with open(path) as f:
        before = f.read()
    after = fn(before)
    if after == before:
        raise SystemExit(f"no change in {rel}")
    with open(path, "w") as f:
        f.write(after)


def config(s):
    if f"  {pkg}: {{" in s:
        return s
    entry = (
        f"  {pkg}: {{\n"
        f'    packageName: "@{pkg}/docs",\n'
        f'    docsDir: "{pkg}/docs",\n'
        f'    kind: "sveltekit-cloudflare",\n'
        f'    zoneName: "{live}",\n'
        f"    hosts: {{\n"
        f'      dev: "{pkg}.21n.site",\n'
        f'      live: "{live}",\n'
        f"    }},\n"
        f"  }},\n"
    )
    return s.replace("export const docsProducts = {\n", "export const docsProducts = {\n" + entry, 1)


def selector(s):
    line = '    if (/^extfn\\/docs\\//.test(file)) selectExisting("extfn");\n'
    new = f'    if (/^{pkg}\\/docs\\//.test(file)) selectExisting("{pkg}");\n'
    return s if new in s else s.replace(line, line + new, 1)


def deploy(s):
    s = s.replace("      - superfunctions-docs-extfn-live-*\n", f"      - superfunctions-docs-extfn-live-*\n      - superfunctions-docs-{pkg}-live-*\n", 1)
    s = s.replace("      - superfunctions-extfn-docs-live-*\n", f"      - superfunctions-extfn-docs-live-*\n      - superfunctions-{pkg}-docs-live-*\n", 1)
    s = s.replace("      - extfn/docs/**\n", f"      - extfn/docs/**\n      - {pkg}/docs/**\n", 1)
    s = s.replace("          - extfn\n", f"          - extfn\n          - {pkg}\n", 1)
    return s


def routes(s):
    s = s.replace("          - extfn\n", f"          - extfn\n          - {pkg}\n", 1)
    ext = "          CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID_EXTFN_COM: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID_EXTFN_COM }}\n"
    new = f"          CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID_{upper}: ${{{{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID_{upper} }}}}\n"
    return s if new in s else s.replace(ext, ext + new, 1)


edit("scripts/cloudflare-docs/config.mjs", config)
edit("scripts/cloudflare-docs/select-products.mjs", selector)
edit(".github/workflows/superfunctions-docs-cloudflare-deploy.yml", deploy)
edit(".github/workflows/superfunctions-docs-cloudflare-routes.yml", routes)
print(f"registered {pkg} (dev {pkg}.21n.site, live {live}, zone var CLOUDFLARE_ZONE_ID_{upper})")

#!/bin/bash
# usage: reset-outside.sh <repo> <pkg> [extra-keep-path...]
# During/after a dev merge: every changed path outside <pkg>/ (and extra keeps) goes back to origin/dev.
set -e
cd "$1"; pkg=$2; shift 2
keep=("$pkg/" "$@")
git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U | xargs -r git checkout --theirs -- 2>/dev/null || true
git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U | xargs -r git add
git diff --name-only origin/dev HEAD -- . > /dev/null
changed=$( { git diff --name-only origin/dev; git diff --cached --name-only origin/dev; } | sort -u)
for f in $changed; do
  skip=0; for k in "${keep[@]}"; do [[ "$f" == "$k"* ]] && skip=1; done
  [ $skip = 1 ] && continue
  if git cat-file -e "origin/dev:$f" 2>/dev/null; then git checkout origin/dev -- "$f"; else git rm -q --cached --ignore-unmatch "$f"; rm -f "$f"; fi
done
git diff --cached --name-only origin/dev | grep -v "^$pkg/" || true

# During/after a dev merge: every changed path outside <pkg>/ (and extra keeps) goes back to origin/dev.
set -e
cd "$1"; pkg=$2; shift 2
keep=("$pkg/" "$@")
git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U | xargs -r git checkout --theirs -- 2>/dev/null || true
git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U | xargs -r git add
git diff --name-only origin/dev HEAD -- . > /dev/null
changed=$( { git diff --name-only origin/dev; git diff --cached --name-only origin/dev; } | sort -u)
for f in $changed; do
  skip=0; for k in "${keep[@]}"; do [[ "$f" == "$k"* ]] && skip=1; done
  [ $skip = 1 ] && continue
  if git cat-file -e "origin/dev:$f" 2>/dev/null; then git checkout origin/dev -- "$f"; else git rm -q --cached --ignore-unmatch "$f"; rm -f "$f"; fi
done
git diff --cached --name-only origin/dev | grep -v "^$pkg/" || true

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Align a DocsFn SvelteKit site's runtime wiring with dev's extfn/docs reference consumer.

usage: align-site.py <repo> <pkg> <DisplayName>
Copies the shared-runtime wiring files from extfn/docs with the product name swapped,
and aligns package.json's test script. Content, landing page and layout stay untouched.
"""
import json
import os
import sys

repo, pkg, display = sys.argv[1:4]
src = f"{repo}/extfn/docs"
dst = f"{repo}/{pkg}/docs"
files = [
    "src/lib/server/docs-site-source.ts",
    "vite.config.ts",
    "svelte.config.js",
    "tsconfig.json",
    "turbo.json",
    "scripts/generate-llms.mjs",
    "src/routes/docs/llms.txt/+server.ts",
    "src/routes/docs/llms-full.txt/+server.ts",
    "src/routes/docs/search.json/+server.ts",
]
for rel in files:
    with open(f"{src}/{rel}") as f:
        text = f.read().replace("extfn", pkg).replace("ExtFn", display)
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(f"{dst}/{rel}"), exist_ok=True)
    with open(f"{dst}/{rel}", "w") as f:
        f.write(text)

with open(f"{src}/package.json") as f:
    ref = json.load(f)
with open(f"{dst}/package.json") as f:
    site = json.load(f)
site["scripts"]["test"] = ref["scripts"]["test"]
for name in ("check:llms", "generate:llms"):
    site["scripts"][name] = ref["scripts"][name]
with open(f"{dst}/package.json", "w") as f:
    f.write(json.dumps(site, indent=2) + "\n")
print(f"aligned {pkg}/docs with extfn/docs wiring")

input.content:
#!/bin/bash
# usage: port-site.sh <pkg> <DisplayName> <branch>
# In the shared worktree: merge dev into the PR branch, keep only <pkg>/, register and
# align the site with the shared runtime, then build/test/verify. Leaves changes uncommitted
# on top of a committed merge so they can be reviewed before the final commit.
set -euo pipefail
S=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
W=/Volumes/Dev/n/sfn-wt/extfn
pkg=$1; display=$2; branch=$3
cd "$W"
git fetch -q origin dev "$branch"
git checkout -q --detach "origin/$branch"
git merge --no-edit origin/dev >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
"$S/reset-outside.sh" "$W" "$pkg"
git commit -q --no-edit
live=$(git show "origin/$branch:scripts/cloudflare-docs/config.mjs" | python3 -c "
import re,sys
s=sys.stdin.read(); m=re.search(r'\n  $pkg: \{.*?live: \"([^\"]+)\"', s, re.S)
print(m.group(1) if m else '')")
[ -n "$live" ] || { echo "no live host registered by the PR for $pkg"; exit 2; }
python3 "$S/register-site.py" "$W" "$pkg" "$live"
python3 "$S/align-site.py" "$W" "$pkg" "$display"
if ! grep -q "canonicalUrl" "$pkg/docs/docsfn.config.ts"; then
  python3 - "$pkg" <<'EOF'
import sys
pkg = sys.argv[1]
p = f"{pkg}/docs/scripts/generate-llms.mjs"
s = open(p).read()
s = s.replace("import { buildLlmsSiteArtifacts, writeLlmsArtifacts }", "import { buildLlmsSiteArtifacts, withSourceLinks, writeLlmsArtifacts }")
s = s.replace("const { artifacts } = await", "const { artifacts, manifest, canonicalUrl } = await")
s = s.replace('writeLlmsArtifacts(resolve(cwd, "static"), artifacts);',
  f'artifacts.llmsTxt = withSourceLinks(artifacts.llmsTxt, manifest, "{pkg}", canonicalUrl);\n'
  f'artifacts.llmsFullTxt = withSourceLinks(artifacts.llmsFullTxt, manifest, "{pkg}", canonicalUrl);\n'
  'writeLlmsArtifacts(resolve(cwd, "static"), artifacts);')
open(p, "w").write(s)
EOF
  if ! grep -q "export function withSourceLinks" scripts/docs-site/llms.mjs; then
    git checkout origin/codex/docs-clifn-20260926 -- scripts/docs-site/llms.mjs scripts/docs-site/llms.test.mjs
  fi
  echo "no canonicalUrl: wired withSourceLinks"

## Set up

1. Create a Discord application and obtain its application ID, public key, and bot token. Set the interaction endpoint to the deployed Worker's `/interactions` route.
2. Create and install a GitHub App for the repositories to expose. Provide `GITHUB_APP_ID`, `GITHUB_INSTALLATION_ID`, and `GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY` to the Worker as secrets. A Linear API key is needed for Linear commands.
3. Deploy the [persistence service](/docs/persistence) if issue-to-thread records are required. Set `PERSISTENCE_SERVICE_URL` to its actual reachable URL; the checked-in `wrangler.toml` value is only a deployment-specific setting.
4. Set `DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY`, `DISCORD_CLIENT_ID`, GitHub credentials, and `LINEAR_API_KEY` as Worker secrets as applicable. Use `botfn/bot-discord/.env.example` for local command registration credentials.
5. Run `npm --workspace @superfunctions/botfn-discord-bot run register-commands`, then `npm --workspace @superfunctions/botfn-discord-bot run deploy` from the repository root.

The registered commands are `link-github-issue`, `create-github-issue`, `link-linear-issue`, and `create-linear-issue`. Autocomplete fetches repositories or issues from GitHub and teams or issues from Linear. Commands add a Discord thread link to the external issue or create an issue with that link.

title: Persistence service
description: Store issue and Discord thread relationships through tRPC.
---

`@superfunctions/botfn-persistence-service` exposes a Hono Worker with a root health text response and tRPC procedures under `/trpc/*`. The service needs `DATABASE_URL` and a PostgreSQL schema matching `src/schema.ts`. The [source setup guide](https://github.com/21nCo/super-functions/blob/dev/botfn/persistence/SETUP.md) provides the DDL for `issues`, `discord_threads`, and the `issue_status` enum.

For local development, set `DATABASE_URL` in `botfn/persistence/.dev.vars`. For deployment, set the secret with `npx wrangler secret put DATABASE_URL --config botfn/persistence/wrangler.toml`. The Worker's `wrangler.toml` enables the `nodejs_compat` compatibility flag with a 2024-09-23 compatibility date because the `postgres` driver needs Node.js APIs such as `Buffer` and `net`; keep that flag if you copy the configuration. Run `npm --workspace @superfunctions/botfn-persistence-service run dev` or `npm --workspace @superfunctions/botfn-persistence-service run deploy` from the repository root. Provision and migrate the database before starting the Worker; the package does not apply schema changes on startup.

- 20.4% duplication on new code: the consumer site mirrors the shared reference site.
